canonicalExplanation.summary: A module decides what the outside world can use with `export`. **Named exports** (`export function parse`) can be many per file and are imported by exact name: `import { parse } from "./dates.js"`. A module may have **at most one default export**, imported under any name you choose. Imports are **live, read-only bindings**: if the exporting module changes a value, importers see the new value, but they can't assign to it. Modules that import each other in a loop form a **cycle**, which can expose a binding before it's initialised.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A dates.js file has twenty helper functions, and every page imports the whole thing through one big default object. Nobody knows which helpers are meant for public use. A utility module exports parse and format by name so callers import only the declared interface. In this lesson you'll organize a feature into modules and diagnose an import or cycle problem.

```predict
{"question": "dates.js has `export function parse() {}` and `export default function format() {}`. Which import is correct?", "options": ["import { parse, format } from \"./dates.js\"", "import format, { parse } from \"./dates.js\""], "answer": 1, "why": "The default export is imported without braces, under any name. Named exports go in braces with their exact names."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know the **Control flow and functions** module, **Module loading baseline** (type="module" scripts), and **Lexical scope and temporal dead zone**, which explains the cycle error.

sections.heading: The model: exports are the module's public interface
Diagnose a cycle

examples.title: A utility module with a clear interface
examples.situation: A utility module exports parse and format by name so callers import only the declared interface.
walkthrough: **Declare the interface:** dates.js writes `export function parse` and `export function format`; MS_PER_DAY stays private.
**Import by name:** a page writes `import { format } from "./dates.js"` and reads only what it needs.
**Check:** a typo such as `import { fromat }` will fail at load time with a clear SyntaxError, instead of undefined later.
examples.result: Callers use only parse and format, and the module's private helpers can change without breaking them.

examples.title: The circular settings import
examples.situation: settings.js imports ui.js to refresh the page, while ui.js imports settings.js to read the theme at top level. The page fails with "Cannot access 'theme' before initialization".
walkthrough: The two modules form a cycle, so ui.js runs before settings.js finishes.
theme is still in its temporal dead zone when ui.js reads it.
Fix: move theme into theme.js, imported by both, so the cycle disappears.
examples.result: Both modules load in a clear order and the page reads the theme correctly.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: A module may have several default exports with different names.
misconceptions.correction: A module has at most one default export. For several public values use named exports; the importer's chosen name for a default doesn't create more defaults.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In the opening predict, why did format need no braces?

analogy.example: A module is like a **shop with a counter**: exported items are on the counter for anyone to take by name; everything in the back room stays private. The default export is the **one featured item** in the window, and you can call it whatever you like when you carry it home.
limitations: Shop items are copies; imports are live views of the shop's shelf.
Two shops that each wait on the other's delivery = a cycle.

steps.explanation: The loader checks the named import against the declared interface.
dates.js runs first, so format is initialised before the page uses it.
The page calls the live, read-only format binding.

trace.textAlternative: Loading a named import. Step 1, Resolve: requested is format; exists is yes. The loader checks the named import against the declared interface. Step 2, Evaluate: dates.js is evaluated once. dates.js runs first, so format is initialised before the page uses it. Step 3, Use: format(date) is '2026-09-23'. The page calls the live, read-only format binding.

nearTransfer.prompt: Split a 60-line `cart.js` into `money.js` (formatPrice), `cart-state.js` (add, remove, total) and `cart-view.js` (render). Write each module's import and export lines.
scaffold: View imports state; state doesn't import view.
expectedEvidence: No import from state back to view.

farTransfer.prompt: Take a feature with a circular import. Draw its module graph, break the cycle by extracting a shared module, and add a test that imports each module on its own.
expectedEvidence: Tests that load each module without errors.

remediation.explanation: For each import ask: **named or default?** Braces for named, none for default. When loading fails with "before initialization", draw the import arrows and look for a loop.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The circular settings import".

recap.summary: To organize a feature into modules, export a small named interface and keep helpers private; import named values in braces and a single default without braces. Imports are live and read-only. Diagnose an import or cycle problem by drawing the graph and moving shared values into their own module.
